summary: The specific R2 citation-fidelity issues at lines 57, 76-80, and 146 are closed: those passages are now clearly marked as summary, memo-level quote, inference, or unverified, and the β.4/β.5 structural blockers remain open with no reintroduced combined-chain or simulation-map claims. However, the draft still contains document-level rigor statements that overstate the citation regime by saying citations are only `[VERIFIED]/[RECALLED]`, which is no longer true after introducing `[SUMMARY]` and `[INFERENCE, unverified]` labels. That keeps the Round 2 major issue open in a narrower but still material form.

issues.description: The rigor statement says citations are marked only as `[VERIFIED against PDF]` or `[RECALLED]`, but the body now also uses `[SUMMARY, not direct quote]` and `[INFERENCE, unverified]`. This overstates citation fidelity at the document-policy level even though the formerly problematic individual citations were relabeled correctly.
issues.suggestion: Update the citation-policy statement to match the actual taxonomy used in the draft, e.g. explicitly list `[VERIFIED]`, `[RECALLED]`, `[SUMMARY]`, and `[INFERENCE, unverified]`, with memo-level quotes described as memo reproductions pending PDF verification.

issues.description: The final rigor summary repeats that citations are strictly divided into `[VERIFIED]/[RECALLED]`, which conflicts with the actual labels used elsewhere in the document. This leaves a residual overclaim about source fidelity in the concluding summary.
issues.suggestion: Revise the summary line so it accurately reflects the document's current citation labeling scheme and caveats, rather than implying all non-recalled claims were PDF-verified.

round_recommendation: Fix the two document-level citation-policy lines, then rerun review; the previously flagged line-specific citation issues appear resolved and no structural regression was found.
